summary: Welaka Fire Tower stands at the Johns Landing Trailhead in Putnam County; one travel blog gives a 100-foot Aermotor-type build in the late 1930s to 1950s and says it is no longer operational.

access.note: Trailhead on County Road 309 with a $2 entry fee per a 2021 trail guide; the tower's stairs are fenced off to the public per a travel blog

visit.trail_note: Stairs fenced off; a seven-mile loop of trails runs through the forest

evidence.supports: Welaka Fire Tower stands directly behind the Johns Landing Trailhead entrance sign
evidence.quote: The steel structure standing directly behind the Johns Landing Trailhead entrance sign is the Welaka Fire Tower

evidence.supports: About 100 feet tall, Aermotor steel lookout tower operated by the Florida Forest Service
evidence.quote: a historic 100-foot-tall Aermotor steel lookout tower operated by the Florida Forest Service

evidence.supports: Build period given by the blog as between the late 1930s and the 1950s
Tower no longer operational; stairs fenced off to the public for safety reasons
evidence.quote: Today, the tower is no longer operational, and the stairs are fenced off to the public due to safety liabilities.

evidence.supports: Blog describes the structure as perfectly preserved (in excellent condition) and an iconic landmark for hikers
evidence.quote: it remains perfectly preserved as an iconic landmark for hikers accessing the Welaka State Forest trail system

evidence.supports: Trailhead lies on County Road 309 just south of Welaka
evidence.quote: The Johns Landing Trailhead lies less than a mile south of Mud Spring Trailhead on County Road 309 just south of Welaka

evidence.supports: Entry fee of $2 at the trailhead

evidence.quote: a series of trails that form a seven mile loop

evidence.supports: Tower list names the site Welaka Tower in Putnam County at 29.45389, -81.65694
Wikimedia Commons places the trailhead in the Welaka State Forest protected area
evidence.quote: Located in protected area Welaka State Forest

evidence.supports: Commons files the tower among Florida Forest Service towers

corrections.why: The record takes its name from the Wikidata trailhead item, but the structure it describes is called the Welaka Fire Tower in the blog and Welaka Tower in the tower list. Keep the trailhead name as an alternate.

sources.title: Sulfur Spring in Welaka State Forest
Welaka State Forest: Johns Landing Trail

notes_for_editor: The build period, 100-foot height, non-operation and fenced stairs rest on one travel blog (Briton on the Move). Its Mud Springs post repeats the same passage (seen in search results, not opened), so it is not independent confirmation. Verify with the Florida Forest Service or the FFLOS before publishing those facts. The tower is not on NHLR's Florida list of 31 entries. The tower list gives elevation 20 with no unit stated. Wikidata types the item as trailhead and fire lookout tower. A YouTube search result said the tower sits at the John's Landing parking area; it was not opened and is not cited. The 2021 date is the trail guide's post stamp. The name correction is a proposal for the editor.
